Subject: Redwood access stewardship kick-off for Highline Bank

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Highline is excited to move forward. We wanted to kick off the access/identity portion of onboarding so we can align on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, IP allowlists, and service account patterns.

Quick context: we have an internal SSO provider (Azure AD) and a central team that manages IP egress (networkops@highlinebank.com). We also have strict org policy guardrails for provisioning production service accounts (least privilege, MFA, KMS key scoping).

Could we schedule a technical kickoff the week of Apr 20? Our asks for that call:
- Confirm SAML metadata exchange and attribute map (email / name / role)
- Agree on SCIM sync cadence and user->group mapping (SSO groups to product roles)
- Provide the expected production IP ranges for allowlist planning
- Clarify naming conventions and KMS policies for service accounts used by Redwood integrations

I've attached a short document with our initial requirements and a spreadsheet of service owners. Please let me know if you want to add anyone to the thread from your side.

Attachments: Highline_Initial_Reqs.pdf

Thanks,
Emily Thomas
Senior PM, Identity & Access

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@highlinebank.com>
Date: Wed, Apr 19 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood access stewardship kick-off for Highline Bank — technical checklist

Thanks Rachel. Adding a short technical checklist for the kickoff so Emily / Highline can prepare items that unblock later tasks:

- SAML / SSO
  - Provide SAML metadata XML or federation URL (IdP metadata). We will send SP metadata back.
  - Confirm attribute mappings: preferred_username (email), given_name, family_name, roles/groups. If you use group-to-role mapping, share group naming convention.
- SCIM provisioning
  - SCIM v2 endpoint and auth (bearer token) or SCIM over mutual-TLS? Please indicate.
  - Expected user flux: initial bulk import (<= 5k users) and daily sync cadence. Include delta cadence expectations.
- IP allowlists
  - Provide production egress ranges (CIDR list) for our allowlist. Include staging ranges if different.
  - Any maintenance windows where we can request temporary exceptions for cutover?
- Service accounts & org policies
  - Naming convention (e.g., redwood-hlb-prod-ssm) and owner contact per account.
  - KMS key scoping: give KMS ARN prefixes and whether key access will be centrally approved.
  - Audit/logging requirements: retention window (days), SIEM forwarder endpoint, and whether egress of logs is restricted to specific subnets.
- Rollout timeline
  - Desired go-live target and blackout dates for cutover
  - Staging test plan: smoke tests and rollback criteria

If Emily can attach the IdP metadata and the CIDR list ahead of the call we'll save time. I'll prepare a minimal SP metadata and a SCIM auth sample to bring.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
